message.content: {"32": {"original": "Leasing software or selling licenses instead of ownership is mistreatment of the", "rephrased": "The practice of leasing software products or selling usage licenses rather than transferring actual ownership constitutes a fundamental mistreatment of the public, as it denies users the control and autonomy inherent in owning their tools. This model must be rejected in favor of systems where long-term possession grants users the right to modify and control the software running on their devices, ensuring they are not held hostage by corporate restrictions.", "summary": "Software leasing and licensing models are rejected as public mistreatment that denies user control."}, "33": {"original": "Any software a user buys must be free, granting them the freedom to run, study, ", "rephrased": "Any software purchased by a user must be free, ensuring they retain the essential freedom to run, study, modify, and share the program without restriction. This requirement applies universally to protect users from proprietary constraints, regardless of whether the transaction involves a physical copy or a digital download, thereby preventing companies from subjugating customers through restrictive terms.", "summary": "All purchased software must be free to guarantee users the freedom to run, study, modify, and share it."}, "34": {"original": "Software must be free, granting users four essential freedoms: to run, study, ", "rephrased": "All software must be free, guaranteeing users four essential freedoms: the right to run the program for any purpose, study the source code to understand and modify it, make exact copies to share, and distribute modified versions to others. These freedoms are non-negotiable prerequisites for ethical software distribution, ensuring that users maintain complete control over the technology they rely on rather than being subjected to proprietary limitations.", "summary": "Software must be free to guarantee users four essential freedoms: to run, study, modify, and share."}, "35": {"original": "Companies impose EULAs to restrict and subjugate users.", "rephrased": "Corporations impose End User License Agreements (EULAs) specifically to restrict user rights and subjugate customers, creating an additional layer of oppression that goes beyond standard copyright laws. These contracts are designed to prevent users from exercising basic freedoms, such as sharing copies or modifying software, effectively turning legal ownership into a state of servitude where users are denied control over the products they have paid for.", "summary": "Companies impose EULAs to restrict and subjugate users, creating an additional layer of oppression."}}
